<description>
This PR adds two JSON-RPC error codes for requests refused by `-rpcwhitelist`, which until now got an HTTP 403 status with an empty body:

- `RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED` (-38) is returned for a refused request, with HTTP 200 for JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and 403 for legacy 1.x requests.
- `RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED` (-39) is returned for the other requests in a refused batch. A refused batch now gets HTTP 200 and an array with an error for each request, and still runs none of them.

**Problem:** `-rpcwhitelist` errors are currently handled differently from other JSON-RPC errors, so clients report them with vague or misleading messages, and for JSON-RPC 2.0 requests the handling does not follow [documented behavior](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md#json-rpc-11-vs-20). Specifically, requests refused by `-rpcwhitelist` get HTTP 403 with an empty body, so the refusal shows up as a generic transport error rather than a specific JSON-RPC error. This is especially a problem for JSON-RPC 2.0 requests, which are [supposed to](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/bf1a1f1662427fbf1a43bb951364eface469bdb7) report failed method calls only as JSON-RPC errors, not HTTP errors. The empty reply causes a concrete problem when JSON-RPC requests are sent over IPC instead of HTTP: `bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect` receives only the response body, so a refused call prints a JSON type error instead of a permission error, as described in a [private security review](https://ipcbugs.ofsky.org/audits/ar-56/). Over HTTP, `bitcoin-cli` currently stops at the 403 status and prints only "server returned HTTP error 403" instead of the actual error.

**Solution:** Report whitelist denials like any other failed call: a JSON-RPC error in the body, with the HTTP status the request's version calls for. This brings the behavior in line with the documentation. `bitcoin-cli` then prints the permission error over both HTTP and IPC, with no change to the IPC interface. The fix is a small change to `src/httprpc.cpp` and `src/rpc/protocol.h`, with tests in `rpc_whitelist.py` and `interface_ipc_cli.py`. It comes after two refactoring commits suggested in #36642, which move connection fields out of `JSONRPCRequest` into a new `JSONRPCClient` struct and move the batch loop into a `ProcessBatch()` helper that the refused-batch reply shares. Details in the commit messages.

Compatibility: HTTP clients that send `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` or batches and check for a 403 status need to read the error code instead. Single 1.x requests keep the 403 status, now with an error body.

Open question for review: `RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED` could be named `RPC_ACCESS_DENIED`, and `RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED` is documented as batch-specific but would fit any request refused before it runs.
</description>

Thanks, you're right. The -39 message listed every denied method and was repeated in each held-back request's error, so the reply could grow with the product of the two. It now names at most three short methods and says how many more there are, so the reply grows linearly with the batch. There's a [new test](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/711222b96fddcf0f5d86e7f4ee3a45942666bbf2/test/functional/rpc_whitelist.py#L187-L195) for it.

[2026-11-12] r:5879493584 review COMMENTED by ryanofsky (member):
Thanks for the reviews!

Rebased 3667e19fe9b189662e9ca4c7931c40d348eb34e3 -> 711222b96fddcf0f5d86e7f4ee3a45942666bbf2 ([`pr/rpcdeny.3`](https://github.com/ryanofsky/bitcoin/commits/pr/rpcdeny.3) -> [`pr/rpcdeny.4`](https://github.com/ryanofsky/bitcoin/commits/pr/rpcdeny.4), [compare](https://github.com/ryanofsky/bitcoin/compare/pr/rpcdeny.3-rebase..pr/rpcdeny.4)) after #36642 was merged:

- Added a first commit with characterization tests of the current replies, so the later commits' test changes only update expected values.
- Added two refactoring commits suggested in [#36642](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36642): a `JSONRPCClient` struct, so each batch element gets a fresh request without copying anything, and a `ProcessBatch()` helper shared by executed and refused batches.
- Bounded the -39 error to at most three short denied method names. Listing all of them in every held-back request's error made the reply size quadratic (reported by [janb84](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36753#discussion_r4526778129) and [Ralph](https://review.fish.foo/traces/36753-3667e19fe9b189662e9ca4c7931c40d348eb34e3-2230-3.html#:~:text=Refused%2Dbatch%20summaries%20amplify%20memory%20and%20CPU%20use)).
- Added a commit fixing `bitcoin-cli -generate`, which ignored errors from `generatetoaddress` and reported success when it was denied ([Ralph](https://review.fish.foo/traces/36753-3667e19fe9b189662e9ca4c7931c40d348eb34e3-2230-3.html#:~:text=bitcoin%2Dcli%20%2Dgenerate%20reports%20success%20when%20generatetoaddress%20is%20denied)).

The other two findings in that [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/traces/36753-3667e19fe9b189662e9ca4c7931c40d348eb34e3-2230-3.html) are fixed elsewhere: [non-object batch elements reusing the previous id](https://review.fish.foo/traces/36753-3667e19fe9b189662e9ca4c7931c40d348eb34e3-2230-3.html#:~:text=Non%2Dobject%20batch%20members%20inherit%20another%20request) by #36642, and malformed 2.0 requests reaching the `Assume()` in `JSONErrorReply()` by #36758.
